THE YMCA OF MONTREAL FONDS ON THE INTERNET ARCHIVE -- WHAT THIS PROJECT HAS NOT READ
====================================================================================
Enumerated 2026-09-07. advancedsearch.php, q="ymca of montreal", rows=1000. numFound 942.

HELD OR CITED SOMEWHERE IN THIS PROJECT: 458.   NOT: 484 (437 images, 47 texts).

A TRAP THAT COSTS AN HOUR IF YOU DO NOT KNOW IT
-----------------------------------------------
The plain-text file in these items is named after the item's TITLE, not its identifier:
  https://archive.org/download/the-news-bulletin-vol-07-no-06/The%20News%20Bulletin%20-%20Vol%2007,%20No%2006_djvu.txt
The obvious <identifier>_djvu.txt returns HTTP 404 with a 146-byte body. Read the file list
from archive.org/metadata/<identifier> and take the name that ends in _djvu.txt.

THE 437 UNREAD IMAGE ITEMS are city-branch photographs with generic titles -- Basketball (13),
Norris Building (10), Gym (10), Gymnasium Activity (8), Day Camp Activity (7), Pool (6),
Swimming Class (5), Hockey Rink (5) and so on. They are NOT catalogued by camp, so a camp
photograph among them would not surface in a search on the camp's name. That is a real
possibility and it is why they are counted here rather than dismissed.

WHAT A SAMPLE OF NINE PROVED, 2026-09-07
----------------------------------------
The News Bulletin, Vol 15 No 1 (1939), carries the table 'WORLD SERVICE OBJECTIVES SUGGESTED
FOR 1939 (As Approved by The Council)', in which CAMP KANAWANA and CAMP OTOREKE are listed as
their own contributing units, among Montreal's branches and Sir George Williams College. The
amounts sit in a separate OCR column run and are NOT matched to names here; do not guess them.
Canadian Manhood (1914-1919) is the association's WARTIME magazine and its 'camp' content is
MILITARY camps, not summer camps -- 45 and 71 hits in two issues, all of that kind.
The 1874 annual report contains the word 'camp' zero times.

CORRECTION, 2026-09-07, ADDED AFTER OPENING ONE OF THE ITEMS
-------------------------------------------------------------
the-quarterly-reporter-1856-01 IS NOT AN 1856 DOCUMENT AND IS NOT MONTREAL'S. It is a JUNE 1944
periodical, Vol. 18 No. 6, which reproduces the Quarterly Reporter's front page as a curiosity. The
reproduced page reads "JANUARY, 1858. NUMBER ONE" and its masthead gives the publisher as the
Confederation of Young Men's Christian Associations under the Central Committee at CINCINNATI, OHIO.
The Archive's 1856 date field is the date of the thing pictured. The 1944 caption is worth keeping:
the Quarterly Reporter "was published from 1856 through 1858 and was succeeded by the Young Men's
Christian Journal. It is the first of the many ancestors of the National Council Bulletin."
TREAT EVERY YEAR IN THE TABLE ABOVE THE SAME WAY -- it comes from the catalogue, and this project
already learned on the YMCA Year Book that a catalogue year is worthless.

THE 437 IMAGES, NARROWED TO 59 WORTH A PERSON'S EYES (2026-09-07)
------------------------------------------------------------------
A title containing a camp or outdoor word is NOT evidence that the photograph shows Kanawana, and
most of these will be city-branch pools, gyms and day camps. The point of the list is that it is 59
items rather than 437. Everything else among the unrecorded images carries a title like Basketball,
Norris Building, Gym, Weightlifting or Model United Nations Assembly.

WHAT WOULD MAKE ONE OF THESE A KANAWANA PHOTOGRAPH: a lake with hills behind it, platform tents,
a council ring, a log lodge. WHAT WOULD RULE ONE OUT: a tiled pool, a gymnasium floor, a city
street. Nobody here can tell the difference, because nobody here can see them.

ALSO NOTE: two titles in the wider set are already-known subjects rather than leads --
"Christieville Ski Lodge" is the association's own ski property, recorded in this project from the
Concordia finding aids and the 1959 annual report, and "In for a Dip - Lake Couchiching" is Ontario,
at Geneva Park, not Quebec.

SECOND CORRECTION, 2026-09-07: THE QUERY WAS WRONG, AND SO WAS THE WORD "UNREAD"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE QUERY. This file was built from q="ymca of montreal", a phrase search, which returns 942 items.
The Internet Archive has a COLLECTION of that name and it holds 1,120. The phrase misses 181 items,
mostly 1962-63 news releases catalogued by their own headline. Almost all of them were already held
in this project by other routes, so nothing was lost -- but the denominator was wrong.
USE  q=collection:ymca-montreal-fonds  AND NOT THE PHRASE.

THE WORD. The table above is headed "what this project has not read". As of the end of 2026-09-07
that is no longer true of the texts: every one was opened. Thirty-two still carry no source record
in this project, and that is because THEY HAD NO CAMP CONTENT, not because nobody looked. They are
the News Bulletin and National Council Bulletin issues that came back empty, the six Canadian
Manhood issues (military camps, deprioritised), and the mis-catalogued Quarterly Reporter.
DO NOT OPEN THEM AGAIN.

CORRECTED POSITION: 1,120 items in the collection; 653 held or cited here; 467 not, of which 435 are
IMAGES and 32 are the read-and-empty texts above. The image half is narrowed to fifty-nine
candidates by title, listed earlier in this file.
